BiblicalUsage: Once, in the judgment on Egypt: When they took hold of thee by thy hand, thou didst break, and rend all their shoulder: and when they leaned upon thee, thou brakest, and madest all their loins to be at a stand. The word is to shake, to make totter, and Egypt is the reed that breaks in the hand of everyone who leans on it.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for shaking carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the picture, that a nation leaned on as a staff breaks and leaves the hand torn.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
